files.description: Daily visitor counts at the north entrance (36 rows, rows not in date order, each day at most once, some days missing): day (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD, September-October 2025), visitors (whole number; equal counts are common), remark (short note; about 47% empty). The dates overlap only partly with footfall_south.csv.

Daily visitor counts at the south entrance (36 rows, rows not in date order, each day at most once, some days missing): day (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD, September-October 2025), visitors (whole number; equal counts are common), remark (short note; about 47% empty). The dates overlap only partly with footfall_north.csv.

task_text: Combine the two files into one table with a column north and a column south and one row per day. Keep the days in the order in which they appear in footfall_north.csv, followed by the days that appear only in footfall_south.csv, in that file's order. `result` should be the first 10 rows of this table, indexed by day.
intended_computation: Take the days of footfall_north.csv in file order, then append the days of footfall_south.csv that are not in the north file, in south file order; for each day give the north and south counts (missing where the file has no row). Result: the first 10 rows of that table (all of them north-file days), indexed by day.

acceptable_variants.notes: the 10 selected days are fixed by the file order. Row order: checked against the requested file order only while the card keeps order_significant true with key __index__ (proposed INTEGRATE resolution); with the flag false, row order is not checked.

predicted_direction.reason: The task asks for file order, which concat(sort=False) gives on 3.x; 2.x ignored sort=False for date indexes and returned the 10 earliest calendar days instead.

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 by pkg:TASKS_M2 for catalogue row R01; naive.py shows the invited idiom, reference.py is the version-robust reference.
